tasks.title: Add Manifest::persist as a required trait method and implement it on CargoToml, PackageJson, PyprojectToml
tasks.reasoning: Rust requires every impl block of a trait to provide every required method in the same compilation unit; adding a required trait method while only some implementors provide it is a compile error for the whole crate. Therefore the trait declaration and all three per-type implementations must land together in this ONE task -- this is the one file-grouping forced by the compiler itself. CargoToml and PackageJson already have a private inherent `fn persist` with the exact required body (cargo.rs:102-113, npm.rs:75-110); this task RELOCATES that function's text from the inherent `impl CargoToml`/`impl PackageJson` block into the `impl Manifest for CargoToml`/`impl Manifest for PackageJson` block, verbatim, with no behavioral change. PyprojectToml has no persist method at all; this task ADDS one, extracting the identical render()+atomic_write(&self.absolute, ...) sequence already used inline by its three mutators, without yet removing those inline calls (that happens in later tasks). Mutator bodies are untouched in this task; write_version/update_dependency_spec/update_optional_dependencies keep calling self.persist(permit) (or their inline atomic_write) exactly as before, so all pre-existing tests remain green. Only the cargo.rs test is added here, since it alone supplies genuine compile-error red (E0576); the npm.rs/python.rs tests are split into T01b because they cannot be red at this point (T01a's single commit already implements persist() for all three types). AC-001 is jointly covered by T01a (CargoToml's direct test) and T01b (PackageJson's and PyprojectToml's).

fix(manifests): guard against CargoToml self-delegation to its own workspace root

When a non-virtual workspace root manifest (both [workspace] and
[package]) tries to update one of its own workspace-inherited
dependencies, update_dependency_spec now returns
ManifestError::InvariantViolation instead of silently delegating to a
WorkspaceCargoResolver targeting the same file the caller will later
persist() over. Defensive: cascade.rs never constructs this case
today (see AC-017). Landed ahead of apply.rs's rewrites-loop persist()
wiring (T04) so that wiring can never observe the unguarded hazard.

tasks.title: Regression test: bumps loop write_version error skips persist and leaves the manifest untouched
tasks.reasoning: NO RED PHASE. This criterion is a structural invariant of Rust's `?` operator (an Err from write_version propagates immediately, before reaching handle.persist(permit)); it holds identically whether write_version self-persisted (pre-T05a) or not (post-T05a), so there is no meaningful red-to-green code transition for this task -- only new regression coverage that did not exist before. No implementation change accompanies this task. The fixture (`package = { ... }` as an inline table) makes current_version() succeed while write_version's non-inherited branch fails, giving a real, reproducible write_version error without corrupting any other invariant. ROUND-4 FIX (round-3 vector-challenger retry, blocking): the prior assertion, `matches!(result, Err(GraphError::Manifest(_)))`, is too loose -- it would pass vacuously for ANY ManifestError raised anywhere in the bumps loop, including one raised before write_version is ever reached (by open() or current_version()), so the test could pass without actually exercising AC-010's scoped claim ("if handle.write_version(...) returns Err"). Read crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs directly to confirm the exact error this fixture produces: current_version() (cargo.rs:166-186) reads `self.document.get("package").and_then(|p| p.get("version")).and_then(|v| v.as_str())`, which resolves through toml_edit's inline-table Item::get and succeeds for `package = { name = ..., version = "1.0.0", edition = ... }`; write_version's non-inherited branch (cargo.rs:218-221) instead calls `self.document.get_mut("package").and_then(|p| p.as_table_mut())`, and `as_table_mut()` returns None for an Item::Value(InlineTable) (it is not an Item::Table), so write_version fails with `ManifestError::MissingField { path, field: "package" }` (the `field: "package"` variant, not `"package.version"` -- that string belongs only to current_version's own MissingField at cargo.rs:184-186, which this fixture never reaches). Tightened the assertion to name this exact error, and added a positive precondition (opening the handle directly and asserting current_version() succeeds) so the test proves it actually reached write_version rather than failing upstream in open()/current_version(). This task remains NO RED PHASE and stays in `red_phase_waived_tasks`: tightening an assertion's precision is not a production-code change, and the underlying propagate-before-persist behavior this test locks in is unchanged by this fix.

Neither phase is expected to interact with this spec's changes in a way the other CI phases wouldn't already catch, but both are part of the justfile's own `ci:` recipe and AC-016 requires ALL of it green, not a subset.
tasks.failing_test: Not applicable -- aggregate verification only, no new unit of behavior.
tasks.expected_failure: N/A: this task has no 'before' state of its own; it runs only after T21a is complete.
tasks.implementation: No code change. Run, in order: `just audit` (moon run :audit), `just doc-check` (RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace).
tasks.expected_pass: Both phases report success: no new security-advisory or license violations from audit, and `cargo doc` builds clean with zero warnings under -D warnings (including for the new ManifestError::InvariantViolation variant's doc comment).
tasks.commit_message: chore(release): confirm audit and doc-check phases green after Manifest persist/mutate split (SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001)

tasks.title: Final gate, part 3: all-features check, wasm-check, coverage
tasks.reasoning: Third and final group of justfile ci phases, per round-3 fix (5). `coverage` runs `cargo llvm-cov --all-features --lcov --output-path lcov.info` (confirmed by direct inspection of justfile line 63) -- an `--all-features` compilation of the whole workspace, including callisto-manifests, that no other phase in this plan exercises. Since `Manifest::persist` is a newly-required trait method, an impl gated behind a non-default feature flag that this plan's author did not notice would compile fine under every other phase but fail specifically under `--all-features`. An explicit `cargo check -p callisto-manifests --all-features` step is run FIRST, before wasm-check and the (much slower) coverage run, so that class of failure surfaces immediately and cheaply rather than at the end of a multi-minute coverage build.
tasks.failing_test: Not applicable -- aggregate verification only, no new unit of behavior.
tasks.test_command: cargo check -p callisto-manifests --all-features && just wasm-check && just coverage
tasks.expected_failure: N/A: this task has no 'before' state of its own; it runs only after T21b is complete. If callisto-manifests has an impl gated behind a feature this plan's tasks never build under, `cargo check -p callisto-manifests --all-features` fails here with a real, distinct compile error (e.g. a missing `persist` method under a feature-gated impl block) rather than surfacing only deep into the coverage phase.
tasks.implementation: No code change. Run, in order: `cargo check -p callisto-manifests --all-features` (new, explicit early-catch step), `just wasm-check` (WASM target cross-compilation and Extism/wasmtime sandbox test), `just coverage` (cargo llvm-cov --all-features --lcov --output-path lcov.info).
tasks.verify_command: cargo check -p callisto-manifests --all-features && just wasm-check && just coverage
tasks.expected_pass: All three steps report success: callisto-manifests compiles clean under --all-features, the WASM cross-compilation and sandbox test pass, and the --all-features coverage build completes and emits lcov.info with no build failures.
tasks.commit_message: chore(release): confirm all-features check, wasm-check, and coverage phases green after Manifest persist/mutate split (SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001)
